entries.core_move: Model the RC low-pass circuit by identifying the series resistor, shunt capacitor, and capacitor-voltage output as the physical LTI filter used for later differential-equation and frequency-response analysis.
Derive the low-pass input-output differential equation from the RC circuit model by relating resistor current, capacitor current, input voltage, and output voltage.
Convert the low-pass differential equation into the frequency response $H(j\omega)$ that maps sinusoidal input frequency to output amplitude scaling and phase shift.
Compute the RC low-pass magnitude response from its frequency response and interpret how it passes low frequencies while attenuating high frequencies.

Model the RC high-pass circuit by identifying the series capacitor, resistor-to-ground, and resistor-voltage output as the physical LTI filter used for later differential-equation and frequency-response analysis.
Derive the high-pass input-output differential equation from the RC circuit model by relating capacitor current, resistor current, input voltage, and output voltage.
Convert the high-pass differential equation into the frequency response $H(j\omega)$ that maps sinusoidal input frequency to output amplitude scaling and phase shift.
Compute the RC high-pass magnitude response from its frequency response and interpret how it attenuates low frequencies while passing high frequencies.

entries.lesson_title: Comparing RC Low-Pass and High-Pass Filters
entries.core_move: Distinguish RC low-pass and high-pass filters by comparing their magnitude-response trends to predict which frequency components are passed or attenuated.
Predict how changing $RC$ shifts the cutoff behavior and magnitude-response transition of RC low-pass and high-pass filters.
